That closes the gap. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/duplicate.html**).

**Duplicate save → edit the existing bookmark** (`shot-35-dupe-edit-existing.png`)
When you re-save a link you already have, the notice now offers a clear **Edit existing** action. Clicking it opens the existing bookmark for full editing — **title, link (web address), description, tags, note, and reading status** — right there, so you update the one you have instead of creating a copy. Saving shows *"Updated … — the existing bookmark was edited, not duplicated."*

**Archived duplicate → both options** (`shot-36-dupe-archived-actions.png`)
If the existing copy is archived, you get both **Edit existing** *and* **Restore it** — it tells you where the bookmark is, never auto-restores, and lets you either edit it in place or bring it back.

And to confirm the normalization: only a **known list** of tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `ref`, …) is ignored; any *other* query parameter is kept as a meaningful part of the link, since it can genuinely change the page. Protocol, `www.`, host capitalization, trailing slash, and `#fragment` are ignored.

Does this fully match your intent for duplicate handling — no duplicates, taken to the existing bookmark with an **Edit existing** action (edit in place, including the link and status), archived copies surfaced with edit + restore, and that normalization rule? If yes, I'll record it — that completes all the behaviours from your original goal, and I'll then move us into checking the edge cases before we talk about building the real thing.
